name: Hidden Costs to Watch for in Los Angeles County Paving Bids

mainEntity.name: What hidden costs should I ask about when hiring a paving contractor in Los Angeles County (e.g., haul-away, traffic control, after-hours work)?
mainEntity.text: What hidden costs should I ask about when hiring a paving contractor in Los Angeles County (e.g., haul-away, traffic control, after-hours work)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many paving bids look similar until additional charges appear during construction. To avoid surprises in Los Angeles County, ask each contractor to explain all potential extra costs. Demolition and haul-away of existing asphalt or concrete may or may not be included in the base price, and disposal fees can be significant. Traffic control, flaggers, and temporary access ramps for businesses or residents often show up as separate line items. If work outside normal business hours is needed to minimize disruption, confirm any surcharges for night or weekend work. Permits, inspections, and required notifications to local agencies may also carry fees. Ask how the contractor handles unforeseen conditions such as soft spots in the base, hidden utilities, or greater-than-expected thickness of existing pavement. Request that the proposal clearly define what is included, what is excluded, and how change orders will be priced. Clarify whether striping, wheel stops, curb painting, and signage are part of the contract or are optional add-ons. By understanding these potential hidden costs before signing, you can better compare Los Angeles County paving bids and avoid budget overruns.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hidden paving costs in Los Angeles County can include demolition and haul-away, disposal fees, traffic control, temporary access ramps, after-hours or night work, permits, and change orders for unforeseen base repairs. Ask contractors to list all likely extras and how they will handle unknown conditions discovered during construction.
